translationRepairs: The Xia dynasty rose through Tushan, but Jie was banished because of Moyi.
The Xia dynasty rose through Tushan, but Jie was banished because of Moxi.
末喜 is the consort Moxi; Moyi misreads 喜 and does not match the established form used in the idiomatic line.
Empress Lü's eldest daughter became the wife of Marquis Xuanping Zhang Ao, and Ao's daughter became Empress Xiaohui.
Empress Lü's eldest daughter became the wife of Marquis Xuanping Zhang Ao, and Ao's daughter became the empress of Emperor Xiaohui.
孝惠皇后 names Zhang Ao's daughter as the empress of Emperor Xiaohui, not a woman whose name is Xiaohui.

Because of their close kinship, Empress Lü desired that the empress bear children by any means necessary. In the end, she bore no children, so she fraudulently took a son from one of the palace women and claimed him as her own.

Because of their close kinship, Empress Lü desired that the empress bear children by any means necessary. In the end the empress bore no children, so Empress Lü fraudulently took a son from one of the palace women and claimed him as the empress's own.
欲其生子 and 終無子 refer to the young empress, while 詐取…為子 is Empress Dowager Lü's fraud; the original she collapses agent and patient.

Therefore, she honored her maternal relatives, enfeoffed the various Lü clansmen as kings to serve as supporters, and made Lü Lü's daughter the consort of the young emperor, wishing to firmly establish and strengthen their family foundation. However, it was of no avail.

Therefore, she honored her maternal relatives, enfeoffed the various Lü clansmen as kings to serve as supporters, and made Lü Lu's daughter the consort of the young emperor, wishing to firmly establish and strengthen their family foundation. However, it was of no avail.
呂祿 is Lü Lu; Lü Lü wrongly repeats the surname as the given name.
Lü Lü and Lü Chan and the others, fearing execution, plotted rebellion.
Lü Lu and Lü Chan and the others, fearing execution, plotted rebellion.
祿 is the given name Lu of Lü Lu, continued from 呂祿 in s0023; Lü Lü is a transcription error.
Only Empress Xiaohui was left dwelling in the Northern Palace.
Only Emperor Xiaohui's empress was left dwelling in the Northern Palace.
孝惠皇后 is Emperor Xiaohui's empress, the same woman as in s0020, not an empress named Xiaohui.

Empress Bo's father was from Wu, surnamed Bo. During the Qin dynasty, he had relations with Wei Fu, a woman from the clan of the former King of Wei, and she bore Empress Bo. Bo An died in Shanyin and was buried there.

Empress Dowager Bo's father was from Wu, surnamed Bo. During the Qin dynasty, he had relations with Wei Ao, a woman from the clan of the former King of Wei, and she bore Bo Ji. Bo An died in Shanyin and was buried there.
魏媼 is Wei Ao, not Wei Fu, but the proposed after still renders 薄太后 as Empress Bo and 生薄姬 as bearing Empress Bo.
Empress Dowager Bo outlived Emperor Wen by two years, dying in the second year before Emperor Jing's reign, and was buried at Nanling.
Empress Dowager Bo outlived Emperor Wen by two years, dying in the second year of Emperor Jing's former era, and was buried at Nanling.
孝景帝前二年 is year 2 of Jing's former era, already two years after Wen (後文帝二年), not a year before Jing's reign.
The following year, her youngest son Wu was established as King of Dai, but later moved to Liang, becoming King Xiaoxiao of Liang.
The following year, her youngest son Wu was established as King of Dai, but later moved to Liang, becoming King Xiao of Liang.
梁孝王 is King Xiao of Liang; Xiaoxiao invents a doubled 孝 that is not in the Chinese.
Empress Dou's mother died early and was buried in Guanjin.
Empress Dou's parents died early and were buried in Guanjin.
親蚤卒 is the early death of both parents, as the next sentence's separate honors of 父 and 母 confirm; mother alone undertranslates 親.
The Marquis of Jiang and General Guan Ying and others said: "If we are to survive, our fate for the moment hangs on these two men.
The Marquis of Jiang and General Guan and others said: "If we are to survive, our fate for the moment hangs on these two men.
灌將軍 supplies only the surname and office; Ying is not in this sentence and should not appear in the literal English.
Zang Er's eldest daughter married into the Jin family as Jin Wangsun's wife, and already bore a daughter, but Zang Er divined for them and said both daughters would be noble.
Zang Er's eldest daughter married into the Jin family as Jin Wangsun's wife, and already bore a daughter, but Zang Er consulted a diviner, who declared that both daughters would be noble.
卜筮之，曰 introduces the oracle's verdict after Zang Er had a divination performed; the original makes Zang Er herself utter the prophecy.
Therefore, wishing to make the two daughters exceptional, she took them from the Jin family.
Therefore, wishing to make the two daughters exceptional, she took the elder back from the Jin family.
奪金氏 reclaims the daughter who had married into the Jin family; 兩女 is the motive, not the object taken, and s0107 continues with a single 之.
When Emperor Jing was crown prince, Empress Bo made a Bo family daughter his consort.
When Emperor Jing was crown prince, Empress Dowager Bo made a Bo family daughter his consort.
薄太后 is Empress Dowager Bo, distinct from the 薄氏女 later made 薄皇后 in s0114.
When Empress Bo passed away, Empress Bo was deposed.
When Empress Dowager Bo passed away, Empress Bo was deposed.
薄太后崩 and 廢薄皇后 name two different women; the original makes the same Empress Bo both die and be deposed.

The eldest princess daily praised the beauty of Lady Wang's son, and Emperor Jing also considered him worthy, moreover there was the previous dream of the sun as an omen, so his plans were not yet decided.

The eldest princess daily praised the excellence of Lady Wang's son, and Emperor Jing also considered him worthy; moreover there was the previous dream of the sun as an omen, so his plans were not yet decided.
譽王夫人男之美 is paired with 景帝亦賢之 in a succession debate, so 美 is excellence or worth, not physical beauty.
As for Empress Wei's sister Wei Shao'er, she bore a son named Huo Qubing, who for his military exploits was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guanjun and held the title of General of Swift Cavalry.
As for Empress Wei's so-called sister Wei Shao'er, she bore a son named Huo Qubing, who for his military exploits was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guanjun and held the title of General of Swift Cavalry.
所謂姊 qualifies the sisterhood as reported or so-called; omitting 所謂 is a semantic loss, not a stylistic trim.
As for Empress Wei's so-called sister Wei Shaorer, Shaorer bore a son Huo Qubing, who for military merit was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guanju, and styled General Champion.
As for Empress Wei's so-called sister Wei Shao'er, Shao'er bore a son Huo Qubing, who for military merit was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guanjun, and styled General of Swift Cavalry.
衛少兒 is Shao'er, 冠軍侯 is Marquis of Guanjun, and 驃騎將軍 is General of Swift Cavalry; Guanju, Shaorer, and General Champion are inaccurate.
Emperor Wu presented wine and toasted her longevity, bestowed ten million cash, three hundred slaves and maids, one hundred qing of public fields, and an armored residence, to grant to his sister.
Emperor Wu presented wine and toasted her longevity, bestowed ten million cash, three hundred slaves and maids, one hundred qing of public fields, and a first-class mansion, to grant to his sister.
甲第 is a first-rank mansion, not an armored residence.
The son was styled Xiuchengzi Zhong, the daughter became queen consort to various feudal kings.
The son was styled Xiuchengzi Zhong, and the daughter became queen consort to a feudal king.
諸侯王王后 is the status of queen to a feudal king; various kings overreads 諸侯王 as multiple husbands.
Lady Xing was styled Jiao'e, people called her "Jiao He."
Lady Xing was styled Jing'e; people called her "Jing He."
娙娥 and 娙何 are Jing'e and Jing He in this chapter's established rendering; Jiao is the wrong reading of 娙.
Therefore, all who bore sons for Emperor Wu, regardless of male or female children, their mothers without exception were reproached to death—can this be said not to be worthy and sage-like!
Therefore, of all who bore children for Emperor Wu, whether the child was male or female, their mothers without exception were reproached to death—can this be said not to be worthy and sage-like!
為武帝生子者，無男女 means every woman who bore Wu a child of either sex; bore sons contradicts 無男女.
She replied, "Judging by her figure, features, and bearing, she is not beautiful enough to captivate a sovereign."
She replied, "Judging by her figure, features, and bearing, she is not fit to match a sovereign."
不足以當人主 is failure to match or befit a ruler, not failure to captivate, but the proposed they are not adequate to a sovereign is awkward.

unresolvedReferences.description: 帝及太子 who were forced to study Huang-Lao are not named; they may be Emperor Jing and his heir or Emperor Wu and his heir.
魏王 is unnamed; which King of Wei the maternal Bo line descends from is not established.
The eunuch in charge of the roster is unnamed and not individuated beyond office.
The Chamberlain for Ceremonials (大行) who petitions for Lady Li and is executed is an unnamed office-holder, not extracted as a person.
Western years for Emperor Wu's court (Lady Yin / Lady Xing episode) cannot be converted from the packet.
Emperor Wu's age seventy at Zhao's birth has no packet Western year.
Emperor Zhao's accession is given only as age five.
Deposition of the Wei crown prince has no Western year.
Early Zhou dates for the Duke of Zhou and King Cheng are not in the packet.
Empress Lü's own early-Han interval is not convertible from this allusion.
